name: NY-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Valdez's large fundraising and outside-spending edge
Republican nominee has raised essentially nothing
model.rationale: The seat's D+25 lean and an open-seat Democratic nominee who has raised $1.7 million with outside support, against a Republican with no visible fundraising, make a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely. Markets price the race near 97% Democratic, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A surprise third-party or independent surge, or an unexpectedly competitive turnout environment in a low-salience open seat, could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Nydia Velázquez (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Nydia Velázquez's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Brooklyn-Queens seat open, but the district's D+25 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic hands on paper. Democratic nominee Claire Valdez has raised about $1.7 million and benefits from roughly $1.2 million in outside support, while Republican Melvin Rivera shows no reported fundraising and no outside spending. An independent candidate has raised only a small amount.

Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 97%, and no general-election polls or expert ratings exist to complicate the picture. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being turnout in a low-profile open-seat contest rather than any realistic path for the Republican nominee.
